title: Two samplers, one schedule: leftover noise

questions.q: What must a correct hand-over set on the second sampler?
options: add_noise disable, the same steps and scheduler, start_at_step at the first's end
add_noise enable and a new seed
questions.answer: add_noise disable, the same steps and scheduler, start_at_step at the first's end
questions.why: Together these make the second start at the noise level the latent really has.

questions.q: What does return_with_leftover_noise disable do on the first sampler?
options: Overwrites its last sigma with 0, so its last step jumps to clean
Nothing unless the second sampler is present
questions.answer: Overwrites its last sigma with 0, so its last step jumps to clean

questions.q: With euler in both stages and correct settings, how does the result compare with one 20-step run?
options: Identical, because Euler has no memory
questions.answer: Identical, because Euler has no memory
questions.why: The lab shows RMS 0.0000. Each step depends only on the current sample and σ.

questions.q: Why is a split dpmpp_2m not identical to a single run?
options: Its previous prediction is lost at the join
It always uses the seed twice
questions.answer: Its previous prediction is lost at the join
questions.why: It reuses the last prediction as history, held in a local variable. A second call starts without any.
